quickFacts.text: Tonight, 21:00: THE FINAL — Spain–Argentina. Kalshi: Spain 43, Tie 32, Argentina 28
Mbappé's Miami brace takes the Boot lead at 10 — Messi needs two tonight to answer
Last night: France 4–6 England — a ten-goal bronze medal and a Saka hat-trick

hero.headline: NINETY MINUTES FROM ETERNITY.
hero.standfirst: It ends tonight. Spain, unbeaten in 38 matches, chase a second star with the meanest defence a World Cup has seen. Argentina, unbeaten in 14 straight World Cup games, chase the first repeat since Brazil in 1962 — with a 39-year-old who keeps refusing endings. And after Mbappé's brace in Miami's ten-goal madness, Messi now needs two goals tonight just to force the Golden Boot countback. Everything, all at once, one last time.
hero.photoCaption: Lionel Messi — one game for the trophy, two goals for the Boot, everything for eternity

briefing.text: The bronze went mad: England led 4–0 at the break through Rice, Konsa and a Saka double; Mbappé led a furious rally to 4–5 before Saka's penalty and Bellingham settled a 6–4 classic.
Mbappé finished on 10 — and, per NBC, his 22nd career World Cup goal makes him the tournament's all-time top scorer. The Boot is his unless Messi scores twice at MetLife.
The Crystal Ball's France call fell in the goal-storm — record now 5 from 10. Tonight, the last regular call of the summer: Spain 2–1. Full workings on page 4.

yesterday.stage: Third place · England take the bronze

facts.text: England led 4–0 inside 45 minutes — then France scored three in eighteen second-half minutes and nearly completed the comeback
Mbappé's brace took him to 10 for the tournament and, per NBC, a record 22 career World Cup goals — the Boot is now his to lose
Saka's hat-trick was capped from the spot in the 87th — the goal that finally broke France's rally

yesterday.report: The game nobody wanted became the game nobody will forget. England buried France in a first-half blur: Rice inside three minutes, Konsa from a corner in the 18th, and Saka twice before the break. At 4–0 the only question was the margin — until Mbappé decided the Golden Boot was worth chasing after all, and Miami got the wildest half of the tournament.
yesterday.report2: Mbappé struck in the 48th and 66th around Barcola's finish, and at 4–3 France were flying. Saka answered from the penalty spot in the 87th, Dembélé made it 4–5 deep in stoppage time, and Bellingham finished the argument in the 97th minute. Ten goals, a bronze for England, and a Boot-race hand grenade rolled onto MetLife's doorstep: Messi now needs two tonight.

star.name: Bukayo Saka
star.line: A hat-trick in an England shirt at a World Cup — two in the first-half storm, and the ice-cold 87th-minute penalty that stopped France's comeback dead.

aside.name: Kylian Mbappé
aside.line: Two goals in eighteen minutes took him to 10 for the tournament and a record 22 in World Cups. The Golden Boot now waits on what Messi does tonight.

yesterday.whatItMeans: England take third, France finish fourth — and the Golden Boot maths is set for the final: Messi needs two to force a countback, three to take it outright.

today.venue: MetLife Stadium, New York / New Jersey
today.preview: The wall against the escape artists. Spain have conceded twice in seven games and strangled France; Argentina have trailed or been level late in three straight knockouts and won them all. Yamal's hamstring has been managed all week; Argentina are at full strength. Messi carries the extra thread: two goals forces a Golden Boot countback with Mbappé, three takes it outright. The money says Spain — 43 to 28 — but a third of $3.9m sits on the draw. Nobody is ruling out the long night.

keyMan.line: A managed hamstring, a penalty won in the semi, and the biggest stage football offers at 18. Win tonight and the era doesn't end — it changes hands.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: Spain are unbeaten in 38 and have conceded twice all tournament. Argentina are unbeaten in 14 World Cup matches — but have needed comebacks or extra time in every knockout round.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: Almost no modern history: one World Cup meeting (1966, Argentina), one 6–1 Spanish demolition in 2018, one 4–1 Argentine friendly win in 2010. Tonight rewrites the whole ledger.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Even: both had the full week. Spain's only flag is Yamal's managed hamstring; Argentina are at full strength but have 330 more knockout minutes in their legs this tournament.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's $3.86m — the biggest market of the World Cup — splits Spain 43, Tie 32, Argentina 28. A third of the money refuses to pick a winner in ninety minutes.

prediction.verdict: Spain 2–1 — the wall bends but doesn't break, and Oyarzabal or Yamal finds the second before Argentina's endgame arrives. But if it's level in the 85th, throw this page away: that script belongs to Messi.
